For neonates older than 7 days and weighing more than 2 kg, oxacillin should be administered at a dose of 100 mg/kg/day, divided into doses every 6 hours, either intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM). 2. Oxacillin reduces the efficacy of live BCG vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. This interaction is contraindicated. 3. Oxacillin decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Systemic antibiotics may act against the vaccine strain, so coadministration should be avoided. Patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination should not receive the cholera vaccine. 4. Demeclocycline reduces the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Doxycycline also decreases the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may interfere with the bactericidal action of oxacillin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Minocycline reduces the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Omadacycline interferes with the bactericidal action of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may reduce the therapeutic effects of penicillins. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Sarecycline decreases the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Tetracyclines may interfere with the bactericidal action of penicillins. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillins if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 9. Tetracycline reduces the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Oxacillin reduces the efficacy of live typhoid vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic therapy. This interaction is contraindicated. 11. Oxacillin and aspirin may increase each other's levels through competition for plasma protein binding or by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Oxacillin and aspirin (rectal) may increase each other's levels through competition for plasma protein binding or by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Oxacillin and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate may increase each other's levels through competition for plasma protein binding or by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Oxacillin decreases the effects of atezolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Oxacillin decreases the effects of avelumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Chloramphenicol reduces the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Azithromycin decreases the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 18. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 19. Colestipol decreases the levels of oxacillin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 20. Erythromycin base reduces the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the effects of oxacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 23. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of oxacillin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the bactericidal effects of oxacillin. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels of oxacillin by increasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 25. Oxacillin decreases the effects of microbiota oral formulations due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may reduce the efficacy of microbiota oral products, which contain bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Oxacillin decreases the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Oxacillin and willow bark may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Oxacillin decreases the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Oxacillin decreases the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Oxacillin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert it to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 35.
